_note: Every tuning number in the prototype. First guesses [MODEL] unless a design doc says otherwise. Section/key are read via GameData.num('section', 'key').

natural_healing._note: Out of combat the health bar refills on its own, for free. It never touches a wound's sink, and never regrows a limb.

reflux._note: Brent 2026-10-12 (design/05 question 2): running hot no longer damages you - skills do not hurt their caster. Above burn_at an affinity's skills take longer to recover from instead: recovery x burn_recovery_mult + burn_recovery_add seconds.

healer._note: The healer sells speed. Wounds first: sink_per_visit points of the oldest wound at price_per_sink_point. With no wounds, health_per_visit points of the bar at price_per_health_point (rest does that for free).

night._note: A night in town: the bar refills, sink_healed points go into wounds that rest can mend (never a lost limb), the arm recovers arm_restored.

town._note: Brent 2026-10-18: corpse runs. Die and you wake in town naked; your body lies where you fell with everything you wore and carried. Walk back for it, or pay corpse_fee_per_star x your stars to have it brought (a flat fee, never a share of what is on it). revive_health_frac: how much of the bar you wake with. The night's rest is a room at the inn - the only rent there is.

wall_recipes._note: design/05 6.2: each wall is a small recipe - a front line, a back line and at most one problem - and no wall introduces more than one kind the player has not met. Keyed by wall number; a wall with no entry uses the nearest lower one. Counts are added to the base rule (grunts_base + wall/2 grunts; brutes by brute_offset/brute_every; a commander at the gate and at the last wall). A pack has at most one Censer-Bearer and one Drummer.

passage._note_owned: This passage is owned (Brent 2026-10-18): it sells tickets and runs a meter (rent_per_s) while you are inside. Wild passages are nobody's and free; public ones are free for low levels. stage_value: the spoils each wall adds.

abilities._note: Stage progress = essence spent x use multiplier, capped at 100. A full bar does NOT advance the stage: it waits for a construct of the matching tier (stage 0 needs a vestige, 1 a remnant, ...). Stage cap = stars + 1. Brent 2026-10-11: skill progress should slow down too, but is left fast for now because it is useful for testing - progress_per_essence is the knob. cast_recovery is the moment after any skill in which you cannot strike or cast again; a skill may set its own 'recovery'.

meditation._note: Meditation gathers wisps (Brent 2026-09-23): refills essence while you sit still. Brent 2026-10-11: it must not work on the move - sitting roots you, and nothing is gathered until you have been still for settle_s.

stars._note: Brent 2026-09-23: you start with a baby star. Each star's capacity grows from a low % to 99%; the essence tank is full_tank x capacity. A new star after ascension starts at 1%. Growth sources are [MODEL]: essence gathered from kills and from meditation. Ascension needs the newest star at max_pct AND the hidden latent aura threshold. Brent 2026-10-11: one star must not hold more than 100 essence, so full_tank is 100 (a full first star is 99); the baby star starts at 20% so it can still pay for one ability. Brent 2026-10-11: the second star came in about ten minutes and should take about two hours, so star growth and the latent-aura threshold were slowed roughly twelvefold (growth_pct_per_aura 0.5 -> 0.04, meditating 0.05 -> 0.005, player.aura_threshold 100 -> 1200, nether.wisp_attuned_star_pct 1.5 -> 0.12). Unmeasured - a first guess at the target.

binding._note: Binding a construct into a full ability (Brent: irreversible, can fail, the construct can kill you). Failure loses the construct and wounds you.

primes._note: Character creation (Brent 2026-10-11): three primes are rolled from the table of playable talents; each then rolls a number of affinity slots - one is common, two rare, three 'VERY VERY rare' - and each slot is filled with a random affinity, unrelated to the talent. slot_weights are the chances of 1, 2 and 3 slots; the exact numbers are ours [MODEL]. talent_weight_by_value makes high-value talents turn up less often. rerolls is how many times the three offers may be rolled again - a testing convenience, set to 0 to make the first roll final.

camera._note: Perspective, BG3-style (Brent 2026-10-18): the mouse wheel moves `zoom` between 0 (far: high and steep) and 1 (near: low and flat, behind the shoulder). Every value below is blended between its far and near end. ortho_size is only for the debug shot modes.

nether._note: The Netherecho [canon concept; every number is MODEL]. The projection is leashed to the body, has very little life, and its death is the character's death. Wisps are gathered by touch; constructs are subdued by beating them down. Sites are the spawn areas a level hands over (one per passage chamber).

wounds._note: Brent 2026-10-11: one health bar plus wounds. A wound cuts the bar's maximum while it lasts and has a hidden pool of healing (its sink) that must be filled before it closes; the sink is never shown in the bar. Everything numeric here is ours [MODEL]. A blow that takes big_hit_frac of your full health in one go, or one that leaves you under low_health_frac, wounds you. sink = the blow x sink_per_damage (at least sink_min); the bar loses cut_frac of full health. max_cut_frac caps what wounds together may take from the bar. wound_cooldown_s stops one flurry from stacking several.

talent_healing._note: Brent 2026-10-11: healing from a talent (lifesteal). Supreme quality (one star): wound sinks first, then the bar. Dynamic quality (two stars and up): the bar up to dynamic_health_first_frac of its ceiling, then the sinks, then the rest of the bar. One heal point is one point of either.

biomes._note: Where a level is set (Brent 2026-10-11: snow levels, dungeons, mountains, cities, swamps...). The kits themselves - floor, walls, gate, props, light - are in scripts/art/biomes.gd. passage and arena are the biomes a delve or an arena visit may roll; town is fixed. props_per_chamber / arena_props are how many decorative props are scattered. Props that block movement are set hard against a side wall and kept blocker_gap metres clear of each other on the same side, because nothing here can path around an obstacle: a pocket between two of them traps a fighter (it stalled the mountain bot run). blocker_collider_max is how much of a big prop is solid. living_prop_kinds are the cuttable props that count as living things (talents that care about harming the living). wall heights are kept low on the camera's side so they do not hide the floor.

ambient_boost._note: Multiplies a biome's ambient light in play. The kits were lit for a staged sample scene; from the game camera the dungeon and the city at night swallowed the player.

shove._note: Water's signature (design/05 2.1): a shoved enemy slides at speed for its distance; if it meets a wall, a block or another enemy with distance still to go it is Crushed - crush_base + crush_per_m for every metre it had left - and interrupted; a body it hit takes crush_other_frac of that. min_left is how much distance must remain for a collision to count. Heavier enemies are shoved less far (enemies.json shove_resist), never zero.

ranged._note: The basic ranged attack (design/06 3.2, smallest version): hold the ranged stance and the strike button fires the equipped ranged weapon toward the cursor. No essence, no reflux, no ammunition yet. A shot does ranged_damage x the weapon's ranged_damage_mult; projectile_speed is how fast it flies; stance_move_factor slows you while you hold the stance; off_arm_damage_factor applies with the striking arm gone. default_* are used when a weapon does not say.

gear._note: Caps that keep gear below the body (design/06 2). armour_cap is the most damage, in percent, that worn armour can take off a hit.

combat._note: Combat rules (design/05 section 6, approved by Brent 2026-10-12; every number ours [MODEL]). POISE: enemies have poise; hits remove it (a bare strike strike_poise, a skill skill_poise unless its payload says otherwise); it refills at poise_regen_per_s after poise_regen_delay_s unhit; at zero the enemy is Staggered (statuses.json). OPENING: a bare strike on a Staggered enemy does opening_mult. WORKING IT OFF: each bare strike that lands sheds strike_sheds_reflux from your hottest affinity. REAR HITS: a hit within rear_arc_deg of straight behind an enemy does rear_mult; enemies turn at turn_rate_deg degrees a second (enemies.json may override) so a back exists. INTERRUPTS: a payload marked interrupts, or a poise break, cancels an interruptible attack and staggers the attacker for interrupt_stagger_s. SLOT RING: at most ring_slots melee enemies stand in striking range of you; the rest hold at ring_wait_distance. PLAYER: you have player_poise; only heavy attacks remove it (heavy_poise_damage each); at zero you are staggered for player_stagger_s - no moving, striking or casting. DASH: after any movement skill dash_recovery_s in which you cannot strike or cast; a second movement skill inside winded_s costs winded_cost_mult essence and reflux.

slipstream._note: Wind's signature (design/05 2.4), only for a character who holds wind: a row of pips earned by moving and lost by standing. +1 pip for every metres_per_pip travelled (walking or dashing); after still_delay_s standing, -1 every decay_s. Wind skills spend pips for their real effect. At speed_pips or more you move speed_mult faster.

stone._note: Earth's signature (design/05 2.3): standing stone. A character keeps at most max_count; raising another crumbles the oldest. Each has hp (worn down by enemy shots) and stands life_s unless the skill says otherwise. It is solid solid_delay_s after it finishes rising, so what it pushed aside has left. An earth skill marked shatters_stone breaks it: every enemy within shrapnel.range of the slab on the far side, inside a cone_deg fan, takes shrapnel.damage and loses shrapnel.poise. All [MODEL].

navigation._note: Pathfinding (scripts/level_nav.gd, nav_path.gd). Every level bakes two navigation meshes from its static colliders: one for the common walker (agent_radius_small covers grunt, archer, harrier, censer, drummer, pavise and the player) and one for the big ones (agent_radius_large: brute 0.8, commander 0.9 - a whole number of cells, since the baker rounds the radius up to one); a walker with a radius above large_from_radius uses the second. cell_size is also the map's cell size. A walker re-asks for its path every repath_s, or sooner if its goal has moved repath_moved metres, and counts a corner reached within corner_reached. A path that ends more than unreachable_slack from where it was meant to go means the goal cannot be reached: the walker stops at the end instead of pressing into a wall. vantage_max_path is how far an archer will walk (by path) to a spot it can shoot from. Structural numbers, not balance.

braced._note: Braced (design/05 2.3): during the wind-up of a skill marked braced you take damage_taken_mult of every blow and cannot be staggered. You are also rooted and committed to where you aimed. [MODEL]

minimap._note: Brent 2026-10-18: a minimap with fog of war in overland zones. The zone is cut into fog_cell_m squares; a square is seen once you stand within sight_m of it, and stays seen (saved per character). size_px is the map's width on screen; its height follows the zone's shape.

art._note: real_bodies: the player is drawn with the real rigged, clothed body (assets/characters/body_<sex>.glb, scripts/art/real_character.gd, dressed by data/wardrobe.json) instead of the procedural one. On since 2026-10-18; false brings the procedural body back. --real-body on the command line forces it on for one run.
